minic.source_equivalence_to_benchmark_source_c: f353826 and 8ce0e5c61ddf7fe2992777b9e6b5c753070e555e match in minic-native, frontend, lower, backend, stdlib and runtime; benchmark branch adds only runner/results files
minic.llvm_target: LLVM C API host triple/data layout; TargetMachine CPU generic; level O2/O3. No target-specific CPU flags.

measurement.timing_tool: existing bench/timeit.c launcher, wait4 child RSS and monotonic wall time
measurement.output_check: every warmup and measured run matched the complete checked-in expected.txt bytes
measurement.counter_availability: no allocation or hardware performance counters collected; RSS/wall only
measurement.fastest_reference: median of correct hand-C O2, O3 and supplemental O3 -mcpu=native variants; Mini ratios use the fastest of those three
measurement.native_cpu_tuning: clang accepts -mcpu=native on Apple M4; no unsafe math; all C variants use -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off

caveats.nbody: C uses static Body[5], Mini uses Array<Body> plus objects; same input, 25,000,000 steps, pair-update/Euler/energy operation order and output. C uses -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off; LLVM API retains default precise FP semantics.
caveats.fannkuch: Same N=11 permutation sequence, prefix flips, parity checksum and max-flips output; C fixed stack arrays vs Mini IntArrays/heap/bounds checks.
caveats.json: Same seeded generation, recursive descent parse/tree walk, REPS=5 and exact output; C uses byte strings and custom buffers/nodes while Mini uses UTF-16 strings, substrings and collection runtime, so treat as a broad workload with representation/allocation caveat.
